rationale: The workflow builds a Gradle Java project on every push/PR across ubuntu, windows, and macOS with no dependency cache, so dependencies are re-fetched repeatedly. Evidence P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (measured experiment batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) shows adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.gradle/caches, keyed by runner OS plus hash of gradle files and gradle-wrapper.properties, reduced median elapsed CI time by ~20.4% while all runs remained successful. Adding that single cache step after setup-gradle and before the Gradle check preserves the existing build/test coverage and required checks, introduces no new network access, secrets, or publishing changes, and satisfies the pattern preconditions (repeated dependency fetching; cache inputs include lockfile/environment) with no contraindication present (no equivalent cache already exists).
